title: IF vs SWITCH: comparisons or exact matches
meta_desc: IF vs SWITCH: SWITCH matches one value against a list of exact cases; IF handles ranges and comparisons. When each is cleaner, plus the default-value pattern.
intro: SWITCH tests ONE expression against a list of exact values — perfect for mapping codes to labels. IF (and its flat sibling IFS) handle ranges and comparisons that SWITCH can't express. Use SWITCH when you're matching equals; reach for IF/IFS the moment you need greater-than.

cols: One expression equal to each case value
States the expression ONCE, then value/result pairs
A final lone argument (odd one out) is the default

when.use_when: Mapping a value to outputs by exact match: status codes to labels, month numbers to names, department IDs to managers. =SWITCH(A2,1,"Low",2,"Med",3,"High","?") is cleaner than nested IFs and names the expression once.
Anything involving ranges, comparisons, or combined conditions (grades by score band, tiered pricing). SWITCH(TRUE, cond1, val1, ...) can fake ranges, but IFS reads better for that.

compat_note: Both execute identically across every LibreOffice version we test; Excel and Google Sheets behavior matches per their documentation. SWITCH needs Excel 2019+ (it's in Google Sheets and LibreOffice throughout our tested range); in older Excel, nested IF or a lookup table is the fallback. For the IF-vs-IFS choice specifically, see that comparison.
